text:
Maya: Heads up — ran into a weird hang when calling list() on a streaming response from the Python SDK while an asyncio loop was running in the same thread. Minimal repro below.
Maya: ```py
client = RedwoodClient(token=...)
s = client.responses.stream(model='rwkv-7b', input='hello')
# sync code, accidentally do: chunks = list(s)  # hangs when there's an active event loop elsewhere
```
Maya: SDK version 0.9.1, Windows and Linux. Happens in our CLI which starts an internal uvloop for other tasks.
Jon: Which transport is the SDK using under the hood in that case? aiohttp SSE?
Maya: It falls back to the async transport, but the top-level API exposes a sync iterator that wraps the async stream. The wrapper seems to block on an event loop check.
Alex: This is an intersection of three things: sync wrapper, async event loop present, and how Python generators propagate GeneratorExit/Cancel. Calling list() will fully consume the iterator and expect it to be purely sync. If the wrapper yields from an async iterator via run_until_complete-like behavior it races with another running loop.
Alex: Repro I saw: if another task has created the loop and you try to run blocking on it, you get a deadlock rather than an explicit RuntimeError.
Maya: Also noticed that when auth refresh happens mid-stream, the SDK silently reconnects but we got a duplicate end marker chunk and then the sync wrapper doesn't close cleanly.
Katie: Oof. We should triage as: 1) explicit cancellation semantics (.cancel() / .aclose()) 2) clear error when mixing sync consumption with a running loop 3) resume token behavior during auth refresh.
Jon: Agreed. For item 2 I think the wrapper should detect if there's an existing running loop in the current thread and raise a helpful error like "Cannot use sync iterator while an event loop is running; use async iterator or client.stream_async()". That avoids deadlocks.
Alex: For cancellation semantics: the sync iterator should implement __enter__/__exit__ and a close()/cancel() that calls aclose() on the underlying async iterator. Also make sure generator.close() results in cancelling the network task instead of just dropping references (to avoid hanging SSE connection).
Maya: Typing request: can we introduce a generic Streaming[T] type so users get iterator/asynciterator hints? Right now the stub is Any which makes typing noisy when you transform chunks.
Katie: Yes — StreamingResponse[T] with Iterator[T] and AsyncIterator[T] unions. Also add Protocols for .cancel/.aclose.
Alex: Another edge: user code doing `for chunk in s: if some_condition: break` relied on __del__ to close network. That's flaky. We should ensure __exit__/__aexit__ guarantees cancellation; and add a warning when destructor closes network (ResourceWarning).
Maya: Minimal fix idea in SDK: if wrapper detects running loop, implement sync iterator as a queue bridged by a background thread that runs the async loop (only when no other loop exists). If loop exists, immediately error. That avoids implicit run_until_complete in user's loop.
Jon: For auth refresh: include a resume token in SSE events. When reconnecting, SDK should resume from token instead of starting over. If token is missing, surface a specific RetryableAuthError that callers can catch and choose to retry.
stream-bot: deploy-notify: new build for python-sdk 0.9.2 published to dev channel (staging tests) :package:
Maya: Nice timing. Can someone from devex add a small sample in the samples/py repo that reproduces the list() hang and a test asserting we raise when a loop is running?
Katie: I'll file an issue with labels: sdk-python, streaming, cancellation, typing, auth-refresh. I'll attach your repro and assign to Alex for initial patch.
Alex: I'll prototype the explicit cancel/close + context-manager patch and add typing defs. If we do the queue bridge it'll be behind a flag and opt-out; prefer explicit error first.
Maya: Thanks — for now I’ll switch our CLI to always consume streams asynchronously to avoid the hit.
Jon: :thumbsup: keep us posted, add any flaky logs to the ticket so SRE can look if same pattern causes leaks in prod.
